title: A One-Parameter, Four-Channel Consistency Test for EFC Background Coupling (β · T(a))
description: Tests a single-parameter Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) background-coupling modification of the Friedmann equation against four independent probes: BAO distances, redshift-space distortions, CMB lensing, and Type Ia supernovae. Finds that a positive background coupling (β ≈ 0.08) mildly improves BAO+RSD fits (Δχ2 = -3.89) while remaining consistent with CMB lensing and SN Ia, and that Poisson-channel modification is excluded by growth data. The transition function T(a) naturally suppresses deviations at high redshift, ensuring GR recovery at recombination and earlier.

modified_friedmann.description: EFC background-coupling architecture: a single parameter \beta rescales the dark-energy term by a fixed transition function T(a) that vanishes as \Omega_m \to 1.

distance_coupling_kernel.description: Kernel defining the standard EFC transition function; it ties coupling strength to the non-matter fraction and suppresses modifications at early times.

growth_ode.description: Linear growth equation; the EFC background modification alters H(a), increasing Hubble friction and suppressing late-time growth.

poisson_channel_alternative.description: Alternative (excluded) coupling route: \mu>1 enhances growth and is disfavoured by BOSS DR12 RSD; EFC favours background (not Poisson) coupling.

key_results.main_finding: Background coupling with a single parameter (β ≈ 0.08) passes four independent probes and yields a mild BAO+RSD preference over ΛCDM, while the Poisson-channel modification is excluded by growth data.
parameters_tested: T(a) (fixed transition function; vanishes as Ωm→1)
datasets_used: BOSS DR12 BAO distances (DM/rd, DH/rd at z = 0.38, 0.51, 0.61)

sealed_predictions.statement: High-redshift Lyα P1D (z ≈ 3) shows a null EFC background imprint (effect strongly suppressed as T(a) → small), delivering no detectable deviation from ΛCDM within current precision.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Lyα 1D flux-power measurements at z ≈ 3 detecting a robust (>3σ) deviation attributable to background-only coupling.

sealed_predictions.statement: Primary CMB anisotropies remain consistent with GR at recombination, as T(a) → 0 implies an effectively null EFC modification at z ∼ 1100.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Next-generation CMB (e.g., Simons Observatory, CMB-S4) detecting a statistically significant early-time deviation consistent with an EFC-like background coupling at recombination.

sealed_predictions.statement: BAO+RSD datasets that probe z ∼ 0.4–0.7 mildly prefer β > 0 with suppressed growth relative to ΛCDM (directional test consistent with BOSS DR12).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DESI/Euclid BAO+RSD combined likelihoods showing no improvement (or a negative preference) for β > 0 and/or favouring β ≤ 0.

sealed_predictions.statement: SN Ia Hubble-diagram residuals shift slightly negative, with |Δμ| ≤ 0.032 mag over 0.1 ≤ z ≤ 1, consistent with mildly smaller distances from the modified H(a).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-precision SN Ia samples (e.g., Pantheon++/Roman) measuring a residual pattern inconsistent in sign or amplitude with the predicted modest negative Δμ.

kill_criteria: KC1: DESI/Euclid BAO+RSD jointly prefer no improvement for β>0 (e.g., Δχ2 ≥ 0 relative to ΛCDM) and/or yield a best-fit β ≤ 0 with >2σ significance.
KC2: Robust (>3σ) detection of a non-null EFC background imprint in Lyα P1D at z ≈ 3, contradicting the predicted strong suppression (practical null) at high redshift.
KC3: Statistically significant evidence for early-time (recombination-era) deviations attributable to EFC background coupling, contradicting the GR-recovery envelope implied by T(a) → 0 at z ∼ 1100.

KC4: RSD measurements at z ∼ 0.4–0.7 favour growth enhancement (Poisson-channel μ>1) over growth suppression with a >3σ preference, reversing the direction required by the EFC background-coupling test.

key_conclusions: Poisson-equation coupling (μ > 1) is excluded by BOSS RSD
EFC enters through the Friedmann equation, not Poisson
β = 0.08 shows mild preference in combined BAO + RSD (Δχ² = −3.89, ~2σ)
Independently consistent with CMB lensing and SN Ia
Four channels, one parameter, zero kills
Regime passes at z = 3 and z = 1100 are automatic consequences of T(a) → 0
architectural_constraint: EFC behaves as a dynamical dark-energy-like background effect, not as classical modified gravity in the Poisson term

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes the first multi-channel empirical consistency test for EFC's background-coupling architecture, demonstrating that a single parameter (β ≈ 0.08) passes four independent probes (BAO, RSD, CMB lensing, SN Ia) while simultaneously excluding the Poisson-channel alternative. It converts the theoretical two-channel ambiguity into a resolved empirical constraint, anchoring EFC as a background-expansion modification rather than a Poisson-term modified gravity. The paper deposits four sealed predictions (Lyα null, CMB GR-recovery, BAO+RSD mild preference, SN Ia residual bound) that create falsifiable hooks for DESI DR2, Euclid, and future Lyα datasets.
graph_insights: This paper is currently an isolated node in the graph (no 1-2 hop connections found), which is anomalous for a paper touching BAO, RSD, CMB lensing, and SN Ia — it should connect to existing BOSS DR12, Pantheon+, and ACT/SPT nodes. The graph likely needs manual edge creation to link this paper to the relevant dataset nodes and to the sealed prediction node for fσ8(z=0.7) = 0.430.

The absence of validation tests sharing observables in the graph suggests that the existing test registry may not have BAO+RSD joint tests or CMB lensing consistency checks catalogued at the observable level — these six new tests should be registered as nodes with edges to the relevant dataset and kill-criterion nodes.

The Poisson-channel exclusion creates a negative-result edge type (EXCLUDES) that should be represented in the graph to prevent future analyses from re-exploring μ > 1 Poisson modifications without acknowledging this empirical constraint.

page_updates.new_text: Four independent cosmological probes (BAO, RSD, CMB lensing, SN Ia) tested against a single-parameter EFC background coupling — all consistent, Poisson channel excluded. Total test count: ~97 survived out of ~107 active (6 new tests added, 1 collapsed). DOI: 10.6084/m9.figshare.31304980

page_updates.new_text: The S8 tension is now addressed architecturally: background coupling (β > 0) produces growth suppression via enhanced Hubble friction, yielding σ8,0 ≈ 0.805 — in the correct direction. The Poisson channel (μ > 1) is empirically excluded as it enhances growth (σ8,0 = 0.879). DOI: 10.6084/m9.figshare.31304980
page_updates.reasoning: The paper provides the clearest empirical demonstration that EFC resolves the S8 tension through background expansion modification, not Poisson-term modification.

implicit_consequences: The Poisson-channel exclusion effectively eliminates an entire class of EFC phenomenology (μ > 1 modified gravity behavior), narrowing the viable EFC parameter space to background-coupling only. This has cascading implications for any test or prediction that assumed a Poisson-channel contribution.

The growth suppression mechanism (enhanced Hubble friction rather than weakened gravity) places EFC phenomenologically closer to dynamical dark energy (w₀wₐCDM) than to f(R) or scalar-tensor modified gravity, which means DESI DR2 w₀wₐ results become a tighter constraint surface than previously assumed.

The sealed prediction of a null Lyα P1D imprint at z ≈ 3 creates an asymmetric kill criterion: a detection would falsify, but a non-detection is necessary but not sufficient — this is a one-way gate that future Lyα analyses must clear.

The GR-recovery margin of 10⁸ at recombination vastly exceeds what any foreseeable CMB experiment could probe, effectively making KC3 (recombination-era deviations) unfalsifiable by CMB primary anisotropies — the real test moves to CMB lensing and ISW at intermediate redshifts.

With β ≈ 0.08 now empirically anchored, the DESI DR2 rapid-response pipeline (identified as the biggest gap) has a concrete numerical target for fσ8 verification rather than a broad parameter sweep — this tightens the pipeline specification.

The four-channel architecture implicitly requires that any future EFCLASS Boltzmann solver must propagate the background modification through the full transfer function rather than treating it as a post-hoc perturbative correction, because the RSD and CMB lensing channels are sensitive to different projection integrals of the same underlying H(z) modification.
ledger_impact.bottom_line_change: The biggest gap remains the DESI DR2 full-shape RSD rapid-response pipeline, but it is now better specified: the pipeline must test β ≈ 0.08 background coupling against DESI DR2 fσ8(z = 0.4–0.7) data, with the sealed prediction fσ8(z=0.7) = 0.430 as the primary target. The four-channel paper provides the calibration anchor (BOSS DR12 Δχ² = −3.89) against which the DESI DR2 result will be compared.
